description:
Biz İnterstellear, Türkiye’den dört kişilik bir öğrenci takımıyız. Takımda yazılım, veri analizi, tasarım ve sunum konularında çalışan arkadaşlar var. Daha önce TUA Astro Hackathon’a katıldık, bu yüzden kısa sürede proje geliştirmeyi ve sunmayı biliyoruz.

NASA’nın açık verilerini kullanarak herkesin kolayca anlayabileceği, çalışan bir uygulama geliştirmeyi hedefliyoruz. Önce basit bir prototip çıkarıp sonra test ederek geliştiriyoruz.
summary: A free browser app that layers NASA data on Gale Crater and plans a safe EVA route to the Mount Sharp boxwork, avoiding steep slopes and rough ground.
details:
Martian Map is a web app for the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge. It combines eight layers of NASA data for the Gale Crater and Mount Sharp area (optical, thermal, spectral, topographic, geophysical, atmospheric, radiation and chemical) and plans an astronaut route between two points.

Key finding: Bradbury Landing to the Nevado Sajama boxwork drill site is 14.6 km. On foot this takes about 6.2 h one way, but only 6 h are usable (8 h EVA minus a 2 h safety reserve), so it is not reachable. A hybrid route (rover for about 14 km, then about 0.5 km on foot) fits the EVA budget. The 500 m vehicle stand-off distance is an editable team assumption.

Safety: the app shows the radiation dose along the route (Curiosity RAD mean 9.94 uGy/h vs solar-event peak 28.8 uGy/h, 2.9x), a slope-based walking speed model (team assumption), and surface conditions from Curiosity REMS (air temperature roughly -87 to +5 C, pressure 644-963 Pa).

Rock avoidance: routes are planned with A* on a 32 m grid. Terrain roughness from the 8 m HiRISE elevation model is used as a proxy for rock formations; the default route skips 5 rough zones. 88% of the route lies on HiRISE data, 12% on coarser MOLA.

Limits are shown in the app: single boulders are invisible at 8 m, HiRISE coverage is about 53%, SHARAD is track lines only, RAD is absorbed dose (not astronaut dose), and REMS is a single station. The app has English and Turkish interfaces and runs in the browser without installation.
projectRefs: Leaflet 1.9.4 (open-source map library, BSD-2-Clause, included in the app)
Claude and Claude Code (Anthropic), AI coding and analysis assistant
Google Gemini, AI research notes about NASA data
Vercel, hosting of the live app
Esri OnMars CTX tile service (source of the CTX mosaic)
USGS Astrogeology Science Center (MOLA elevation mosaic)
University of Arizona HiRISE (PDS archive for terrain models)
Playwright (testing and screenshots only, not part of the app)
